subject: POC Observability Plan and Success Criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechx.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: POC Observability Plan and Success Criteria

Hi Sam / Priya,

Great to meet you both on the call today — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the FintechX POC focused on observability so we can evaluate performance, cost, and reliability during the trial: 

High-level success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for typical user flows (50-200 tokens).
- Error tolerance: visible error rate < 0.5% for inference requests.
- Cost visibility: per-route token cost and projected monthly spend within agreed limits.
- Quality: output quality comparable to your current baseline for the same prompts (we'll define 10 eval prompts).

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline:
- Week 1: Provision POC environment (hosted dedicated pool) + enable tracing and logs export.
- Week 2: Run synthetic load and record metrics; FintechX runs eval prompts.
- Week 3: Joint review, iterate on batching/quantization settings, finalize recommendations.

Ownership (suggested):
- Redwood: infra setup, dashboard templates in Redwood Console, tracing and prefix/KV cache config.
- FintechX: provide eval prompt set, product flows to test, access to Datadog/Grafana for export.

Observability items we plan to enable for the POC (details attached in POC-Observability-Requirements.pdf):
- Dashboards: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), error rates, throughput, token usage, per-route cost.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces capturing request-id, model variant, routing decisions, and infra hops.
- Logs: request metadata (redacted user IDs), response size, token counts; export to S3/FintechX logging endpoint.
- Alerts: high error rate, sustained p95 degradation, cache miss spikes, GPU throttling.

Can you confirm the success criteria above and the proposed owners/timeline? If that works I'll loop in engineering to schedule the kickoff for week of Mar 9.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachments: POC-Observability-Requirements.pdf

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan and Success Criteria

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming that the high-level criteria look good from our side. A few clarifications / asks from FintechX: 

- Latency: p95 target is acceptable as long as we can see the histogram by route. Some routes are 1-2x longer due to prompt length; we'll flag those.
- Quality: we'll share a 10-prompt eval sheet (attached) and will include some edge cases.
- Data/export: we need logs exported to our S3 bucket with daily rollover and 90-day retention. Can Redwood support that?
- Monitoring: prefer to ingest Redwood metrics into Datadog (API key will be shared with your infra team).

Owners from our side:
- Sam Patel — overall POC owner (I will be the exec sponsor).
- Priya Rao — lead on evaluation & prompts.
- Devops: Ramesh Kumar <ramesh.k@fintechx.com> — will coordinate S3/Datadog access.

Timeline: happy with proposed weeks; we can do kickoff Mar 9. Please confirm the specific infra requirements (GPU types / network egress constraints) so Ramesh can provision access.

I've attached our evaluation checklist (FintechX-eval-criteria.xlsx).

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Head of Data Platform | FintechX
sam.patel@fintechx.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan and Success Criteria (internal)

Looping you both in — couple of notes from engineering side based on Sam's asks: 

- S3 export: We can push structured logs (JSON per request) to FintechX S3 via a signed IAM role / presigned URLs. Retention is controlled by FintechX lifecycle rules; we'll confirm format.
- Datadog: We'll expose Redwood metrics via push endpoint / statsd; need the API key and target namespace. Also can wire up a managed Grafana dashboard pointing to the same metrics.
- Tracing: We'll instrument request traces with a request_id and add spans for routing/model selection and GPU queue wait time. Will need finite sampling (10-20%) to avoid cost blowup.

Action items (internal):
1) Aditya: prepare the dashboard templates and sample Grafana/Datadog dashboards (latency histogram, token cost, cache hit/miss, GPU_util).
2) Marcus: confirm POC infra footprint (recommended GPU types and estimated token/sec for synthetic load).
3) Marissa: confirm kickoff date and get Datadog key + S3 bucket name / access contact from FintechX.

I can pick up the tracing instrumentation and log format doc; will share the draft by end of day Mar 5.

-Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechx.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan and Success Criteria — confirmed plan & next steps

Thanks Sam — confirming kickoff week of Mar 9 works for us. Finalized plan and owners below. I've attached Redwood's observability playbook for reference.

Final POC observability checklist (what Redwood will deliver):
- Dashboards (Redwood Console + Grafana/Datadog exports):
  - Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 by route, latency histogram, avg token processing time.
  - Errors: error rate by route, top error messages (sampled).
  - Throughput & cost: rps, tokens/sec, per-route token cost & cumulative spend estimate.
  - Cache & batching: prefix/KV cache hit rate, batching size distribution, queue_depth.
- Tracing:
  - End-to-end traces with request_id, spans for routing/model-variant selection, queue wait, model inference time.
  - Sampling: default 10% for traces; can increase for specific flows.
- Logs & exports:
  - Structured request logs (redacted PII) exported daily to FintechX S3 (format: JSONL, gzip).
  - Retention: we'll hand off to FintechX lifecycle rules (you requested 90 days).
- Alerts & runbook:
  - Alerts for sustained p95 > 350ms, error_rate > 0.5%, cache_miss_rate spike > 15%.
  - Runbook with triage steps will be provided during week 2 review.

Responsibilities / contacts:
- Redwood: Jordan (tracing + logs format), Aditya (dashboards), Marcus (infra sizing).
- FintechX: Sam (POC sponsor), Priya (evaluation), Ramesh (S3/Datadog access).

Next steps: 
1) Sam / Ramesh: share Datadog API key and S3 bucket name, or add the Redwood service account with write permissions (Ramesh contact).
2) Aditya: share dashboard templates by EOD Mar 5.
3) Jordan: send tracing/log format doc by EOD Mar 5.
4) Mar 9: kickoff call to confirm access and run synthetic load test plan.

If that all looks good I'll send a calendar invite for Mar 9 10:00am PT and open the POC in HubSpot (HS-234567).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
